compiled:
📰 General

Dexter Lawrence Promises Fire and Fury as Bengals Embrace New Star •

Bengals president Mike Brown greeted defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II following his recent arrival, noting the player’s enthusiastic energy. Lawrence emphasized his commitment to the team, stating he understands the significant investment made by the Bengals organization. The defensive tackle expressed a desire to ignite a winning culture within the team. Lawrence’s arrival is being viewed positively by the Bengals fanbase, who recognize the value he brings to the roster.

🌍 World

Hamas Announces Readiness to Hand Over Weapons to Israel •

Hamas officials have stated the group is prepared to transfer thousands of automatic rifles and other weapons from its internal security forces in Gaza. This move represents a significant shift in strategy by Hamas, previously resistant to relinquishing arms. The transfer would involve weapons belonging to the Hamas police force and other internal security services. The announcement comes amid ongoing negotiations and heightened tensions between Hamas and Israel.

🦅 US

Iowa City Shooting Leaves Five Wounded Near University of Iowa Ped Mall •

Five individuals were injured in a shooting that occurred in the downtown Iowa City Ped Mall early Sunday morning. The incident stemmed from a dispute that escalated into violence within the nightlife district adjacent to the University of Iowa campus. Police and university officials confirmed that three students were among the victims transported to local hospitals for treatment. Investigations are currently underway to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting and identify those involved.

💰 Business

Trump-Appointed Energy Secretary Faces Scrutiny Over Gas Price Claims •

Energy Secretary Christopher Wright faced questioning regarding his inconsistent statements about rising gasoline prices. Appearing on CNN’s “State of the Union,” Wright was confronted by host Jake Tapper about previous predictions. The appearance followed Wright’s shifting narratives concerning the impact of the ongoing conflict in Iran on fuel costs. The questioning highlighted discrepancies in his public statements and raised concerns about the accuracy of information provided by the Department of Energy.

💻 Technology

YouTuber Successfully Recreates Nintendo’s Lost, Ultra-Rare Arcade Game •

A YouTuber has meticulously reconstructed Nintendo’s Wild Gunman, a notoriously rare and elusive arcade game from the company’s early history. The project involved extensive research, sourcing original schematics, and utilizing 3D printing to recreate the game’s components. Wild Gunman was one of Nintendo’s first arcade titles, released in 1972, and was incredibly difficult to find and play due to limited production and subsequent loss. The YouTuber’s successful recreation offers a fascinating glimpse into Nintendo’s pre-video game origins and highlights the rarity of this forgotten title.

🎭 Entertainment

Zendaya Dominates Met Gala, Showcasing Stunning Custom Valentino Gown •

Zendaya graced the 2024 Met Gala with a breathtaking custom Valentino Haute Couture gown designed by Pierpaolo Piccioli. The dress featured a dramatic, floor-length silhouette with intricate embellishments and a deep V-neckline. She accessorized with Tiffany & Co. jewelry and a stunning diamond bracelet. The event celebrated the theme "Sleeping Beauties: Reawakening Fashion," and Zendaya’s appearance was widely considered a standout moment.

🏅 Sports

Yankees Weather Rain Delay, Secure Second Consecutive Victory Over Royals •

The New York Yankees postponed their game against the Kansas City Royals on April 19th due to inclement weather. Play was initially scheduled for 6:40 PM EST but was ultimately suspended due to persistent rain and thunderstorms. Prior to the delay, the Yankees had secured a 2-0 lead in the contest, capitalizing on a performance where Mike Trout was unable to contribute. The game was expected to resume at a later date, with details to be announced by the teams.

🔬 Science

Physicists Propose Universe Originated From Black Hole “Bounce,” Challenging Big Bang •

A team at the University of Portsmouth has developed a new theory suggesting the universe’s creation wasn’t a singular explosion, but rather a “bounce” triggered by a massive, ancient black hole. This model proposes that the universe emerged from the collapse and subsequent rebound of this primordial black hole. The theory suggests the initial expansion wasn’t driven by the Big Bang, but by this cyclical event. Researchers are currently investigating the implications of this model for understanding the universe’s earliest moments.

🩺 Health

Utah Becomes America’s New Measles Epicenter, With Over 600 Cases Reported •

Utah has become the primary location of a measles outbreak in the United States, according to data from the state’s health department. As of this week, the outbreak has recorded over 600 confirmed cases. The majority of these cases, totaling more than 400, were identified between January and April. Health officials are investigating the source of the outbreak and urging residents to get vaccinated to prevent further spread of the highly contagious disease.
